# Google Play

11 endpoints, all GET. Base URL `https://www.socialcrawl.dev`, auth header `x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY`.

**Credit costs:** 6 standard (1 credit), 3 advanced (5), 1 premium (10), 1 custom (flat/metered) - the exact cost is in each endpoint heading below.

## GET /v1/google_play/app-info - 5 credits (advanced)

Returns the full canonical `App` record for one Google Play app keyed by its package name (`app_id`): title, description, developer block (incl. email/address/website), rating, price, install count + display ('1,000,000,000+'), version, size, screenshots, genres, chart tags, similar apps, and update date. The `app.store` field is always "google_play"; Apple-only leaves (advisories, languages) are null. Get the `app_id` from /v1/google_play/app-search. Text leaves (`title`, `description`, `update_notes`) are decoded from the store's HTML escaping; the store's raw text stays in `app.ext.appdata`. `update_notes` is null when the listing sends no What's new text. `installs` is null, with a `_warnings` line, when the store lists fewer installs than the app has ratings (a preinstalled app such as Google Recorder shows "1+"); the store's figure stays in `app.ext.appdata.installs`. `rating.count` is the app's worldwide number of ratings, so it is the same in every `country`, while `rating.value` is that storefront's own average. `price.displayed` is filled only when the store sends a display price, which it does not for free apps; this source carries no in-app purchase or contains-ads data.

**Use when** you already have an app_id and need the detail that search results leave out.
**Cost** cache 600 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Paging** none

**Query params**

- `app_id` (required) - Google Play package name (e.g. 'com.spotify.music'), from app-search. · e.g. `com.spotify.music`
- `country` (optional, string) - Storefront country as an ISO code ('US'), a full name, or a numeric code. Defaults to the US. · e.g. `United States`
- `language` (optional, string) - Language code (e.g. 'en'). Defaults to 'en'.

**Response** `App` object at `data`, `{ app }` ([full schema](schemas/App.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `app.id` | Store app ID… |
| `app.title` | App title |
| `app.url` | URL of the app's store page. |
| `app.developer.id` | The store's id for the developer. |
| `app.developer.name` | Developer or publisher name. |
| `app.developer.url` | URL of the developer's page in the store. |

+23 more (types in the full schema): `app` {category, description, icon, minimum_os_version, released_at, reviews_count, size, store, subtitle, update_notes, updated_at, version}; `app.developer` {address, email, website}; `app.price` {currency, current, displayed, is_free} (+4 more).

**Next** `google_play/app-reviews` (`app_id` ← `data.app.id`) - Get Google Play reviews for an app.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/google_play/app-info" \
  --data-urlencode "app_id=com.spotify.music" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/google_play/app-list - 5 credits (advanced)

Returns a unified AppList for a Google Play store chart (top free, top paid, top grossing, movers & shakers, etc.), optionally scoped to a category. Each item is the same canonical `App` shape as app-search, and `app.rank` is its position in the chart (1 is the top), in the order the items arrive. Use it to track ranking movements or build a category leaderboard. A chart row carries the title, icon, developer name, store URL, price and free flag, and the star rating (`app.rating.value`) where the storefront publishes it. `app.reviews_count` and `app.rating.count` are not sent on chart rows in any storefront and are always null here; read them from /v1/google_play/app-info. Some storefronts send no star rating on chart rows at all: on 19/10/2026 the South African (`country=ZA`) top free chart had no rating on 100 of 100 apps, while Nigeria had a rating on all 100 and Kenya on 98. When no app on the page has a rating, `_warnings` carries `ratings_unavailable`, so an empty rating column is never mistaken for zero; /v1/google_play/app-info returns the rating for one app in that storefront. `app.ext.appdata` is the store's raw row, kept for reference; read the unified leaves above it first.

**Use when** you want to track ranking movements or build a category leaderboard, rather than searching for one named app.
**Cost** cache 120 s
**Paging** single page - Depth-based fan-out: page size is controlled by depth, one call.

**Query params**

- `app_collection` (required) - Chart to retrieve: topselling_free, topselling_paid, topgrossing, movers_shakers, topselling_new_free, topselling_new_paid. An unknown value is rejected with a free 400 that lists the accepted set. · e.g. `topselling_free`
- `app_category` (optional, enum: art_and_design | auto_and_vehicles | beauty | books_and_reference | business | comics | communication | dating | education | entertainment | events | finance | food_and_drink | health_and_fitness | house_and_home | libraries_and_demo | lifestyle | maps_and_navigation | medical | music_and_audio | news_and_magazines | parenting | personalization | photography | productivity | shopping | social | sports | tools | travel_and_local | video_players | android_wear | watch_face | weather | game | game_action | game_adventure | game_arcade | game_board | game_card | game_casino | game_casual | game_educational | game_music | game_puzzle | game_racing | game_role_playing | game_simulation | game_sports | game_strategy | game_trivia | game_word | family) - Optional Google Play category to scope the chart (e.g. 'photography', 'game_puzzle'). · e.g. `photography`
- `country` (optional, string) - Storefront country as an ISO code ('US'), a full name, or a numeric code. Defaults to the US.
- `language` (optional, string) - Language code (e.g. 'en'). Defaults to 'en'.
- `depth` (optional, integer) - Number of apps to retrieve (default 100, rounded up to multiples of 100, max 500). The store decides how deep a chart actually goes: measured 06/09/2026, `topselling_free` returns 100 at the default and 200 at depth=500, and `topselling_new_paid` has only 5 apps in it. · e.g. `100`

**Constraints**

- `app_collection`: at most 1 comma-separated values; each value one of topselling_free | topselling_paid | topgrossing | movers_shakers | topselling_new_free | topselling_new_paid.

**Response** `AppList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ app }` ([full schema](schemas/AppList.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `app.id` | Store app ID… |
| `app.title` | App title |
| `app.url` | URL of the app's store page. |
| `app.developer.id` | The store's id for the developer. |
| `app.developer.name` | Developer or publisher name. |
| `app.developer.url` | URL of the developer's page in the store. |

+21 more (types in the full schema): `app` {category, description, icon, minimum_os_version, released_at, size, store, subtitle, update_notes, updated_at, version}; `app.developer` {address, email, website}; `app.price` {currency, current, displayed, is_free, original} (+2 more). Never filled: `app.rating.count`, `app.reviews_count`. Page-level: `data.dropped`, `data.empty_reason`, `data.empty_reason_note`.

**Next** `google_play/app-info` (`app_id` ← `data.items[].app.id`) - Get full Google Play app details.

## GET /v1/google_play/app-listings-search - 10 credits (premium)

Searches a real-time, filterable Google Play listings database by app title (and/or description) and returns a unified AppList. Unlike the store-chart endpoints this one is the ONE true paginator: page by passing `pagination.next_cursor` back as `cursor` until `pagination.has_more` is false, size the page with `limit` (≤50), and read the platform-wide match count at `data.total` (14,686 for the query 'photo editor' on 06/09/2026). Each row also carries `app.ext.appdata.time_update`, the freshness stamp for that listing in the database. Premium-tier because this surface is billed per returned item.

**Use when** you must page through many results, since it is the only Google Play endpoint with real paging.
**Cost** cache 120 s
**Paging** cursor (native `offset_token`) · ≈20/page (observed once); set with `limit` · depth unknown · N items ≈ ceil(N/20) x 10 credits · typical 0.7-0.7 s

**Query params**

- `title` (required) - App title to search for (e.g. 'photo editor'). · e.g. `photo editor`
- `description` (optional, string) - Optional app-description text to match.
- `limit` (optional, integer) - Apps per page (1-50, default 20). · e.g. `20`
- `offset` (optional, integer) - Pagination offset (up to 10,000). Prefer `cursor`: pass `pagination.next_cursor` straight back and the offset is handled for you.
- `offset_token` (optional, string) - Legacy deep-pagination token. Prefer `cursor`, which accepts `pagination.next_cursor` verbatim and works on every paginatable endpoint.
- `filters` (optional, string) - Advanced filter expression as a JSON array of clauses, e.g. [["item.rating.value",">",4]]. Must be valid JSON and must be an array: anything else is rejected with a free 400 rather than silently returning an unfiltered page. · e.g. `[["item.rating.value",">",4]]`
- `country` (optional, string) - Storefront country as an ISO code ('US'), a full name, or a numeric code. Defaults to the US.
- `language` (optional, string) - Language code (e.g. 'en'). Defaults to 'en'.
- **Shared controls** `max_pages` (1-50) → [walks](api-overview.md#search-filters-and-multi-page-walks); `max_items` (1-5000) · `max_credits` (1-100000) → [one-call walks](api-overview.md#get-more-in-one-call-max_items-max_credits-max_pages)

**Response** `AppList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ app }` ([full schema](schemas/AppList.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `app.id` | Store app ID… |
| `app.title` | App title |
| `app.url` | URL of the app's store page. |
| `app.developer.id` | The store's id for the developer. |
| `app.developer.name` | Developer or publisher name. |
| `app.developer.url` | URL of the developer's page in the store. |

+23 more (types in the full schema): `app` {category, description, icon, minimum_os_version, released_at, reviews_count, size, store, subtitle, update_notes, updated_at, version}; `app.developer` {address, email, website}; `app.price` {currency, current, displayed, is_free} (+4 more). Page-level: `data.dropped`, `data.empty_reason`, `data.empty_reason_note`, `data.walk`.

**Next** `google_play/app-reviews` (`app_id` ← `data.items[].app.id`) - Get Google Play reviews for an app. · `google_play/app-info` (`app_id` ← `data.items[].app.id`) - Get full Google Play app details.

## GET /v1/google_play/app-reviews - 5-9 credits (request-shaped)

Returns a unified ReviewList of Google Play user reviews for an app, keyed by its package name (`app_id` on every review's `entity_id`). Each review carries the star rating, full text, reviewer name + avatar, helpful-vote count, developer `responses[]` (reply text + date), publish date, and `url`, the review's own page on Google Play (built from the app id and the review id, so a quote can be cited): on the SAME canonical `Review` shape used by Amazon, Google Shopping, and Trustpilot. Google reviews have no title (always null). `depth` returns reviews in batches of 150 and rounds up to the next batch (depth=200 returns up to 300), at most 600, all in one call for 5 credits.

**Use when** you want to read what users say about one app; reviews come back in batches of 150, up to 600 in total. **Not for** both stores at once with themes and sentiment over time (prism/app-reviews).
**Cost** price moves with `label` · cache 300 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Pricing** 5 credits a call at any `depth` up to 600: one call returns every batch of 150 it asks for, so 600 reviews cost 5, not 20. The default labels (sentiment, issue) are free. label=reports, incentivized or injection holds 4 extra credits and refunds down to 1 credit per started 25 reviews that were newly judged (the first 100 reviews of a page are judged): reviews already labelled are free, a page where nothing could be judged refunds the whole extra, and a cached page is free.
**Paging** single page - Depth-based fan-out: page size is controlled by depth, one call.

**Query params**

- `app_id` (required) - Google Play package name (e.g. 'com.spotify.music'), from app-search. · e.g. `com.spotify.music`
- `country` (optional, string) - Storefront country as an ISO code ('US'), a full name, or a numeric code. Defaults to the US.
- `language` (optional, string) - Language code (e.g. 'en'). Defaults to 'en'.
- `depth` (optional, integer) - Number of reviews to retrieve (default 150, rounded up to a multiple of 150, max 600). One call at any depth costs 5 credits. · e.g. `150`
- `sort_by` (optional, enum: newest | most_relevant) - Review ordering: `newest` (default) or `most_relevant`. The App Store's `most_recent` and `mostRecent` are read as `newest`, with a `_warnings` line. · e.g. `newest`
- `rating` (optional, integer) - Filter to a single star rating (1-5). Verified working on this store (measured 06/09/2026: `rating=5` returns 150 five-star reviews, `rating=1` returns 150 one-star). The Apple App Store has no equivalent filter upstream.
- `since` (optional, string) - Rows published from this date: YYYY-MM-DD (midnight UTC) or ISO 8601. Rows older than it are left off the page, and the page that reaches one ends the walk: `next_cursor` is not returned and `pagination.stopped_at` is `since`. Sending it sets the newest-first sort shown in this endpoint's sort parameter (any other sort value is a free 400). The page still costs what a page costs, so you pay for the pages you walk and no more. Aliases: [date window](api-overview.md#date-window-since-until).
- **Shared controls** `label` (sentiment | issue | reports | incentivized | injection; paid: reports, incentivized, injection) · `label_evidence` (1) · `reports` → [labels](api-overview.md#labels-relevance-and-quality); `until` → [date window](api-overview.md#date-window-since-until)

**Constraints**

- `since` requires `sort_by=newest` (auto-injected when `sort_by` is absent; a different value is a free 400).
- `reports`, `label_evidence` are no-ops without `label` - sending one alone is a free 400.
- `goal`, `fit_tokens` are no-ops without `fit` - sending one alone is a free 400.
- `label`: at most 5 comma-separated values.

**Response** `ReviewList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ computed, review }` ([full schema](schemas/ReviewList.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `review.text` | Full review body |
| `review.id` | Review ID (parsed from the review URL when not first-class) |
| `review.published_at` | Review creation timestamp as an ISO 8601 UTC string… |
| `review.author.name` | Reviewer name. |
| `computed.labels_evidence` | When 1, every labelled row also carries… (with `label_evidence=1`) |
| `review.entity_id` | ID of the reviewed entity… |

+9 more (types in the full schema): `review` {helpful_votes}; `computed.labels` {incentivized, injection, issue, reports, sentiment}; `review.author` {avatar_url}; `review.rating` {max, value}. Also in the sample: `review` {url null, verified null, source null, language null, original_language null, translated null, images null}; `review.author` {url null, location null, reviews_count null} (+27 more). Empty on every row the field-health check sampled (22/11/2026), so not returned today: `review.title`. Page-level: `data.dropped`, `data.empty_reason`, `data.empty_reason_note`, `data.estimate`, `data.held_back`, `data.labels`.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/google_play/app-reviews" \
  --data-urlencode "app_id=com.spotify.music" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/google_play/app-search - 5 credits (advanced)

Returns a unified AppList of Google Play apps matching a keyword: title, icon, developer, rating, price/is_free, and store URL on every item, on the same canonical `App` shape used across every app marketplace (`app.store` = "google_play"). `app.rank` is the position of the app in the results (1 is the first). Detail-only fields (description, screenshots, installs) are null on search items; fetch /v1/google_play/app-info for the full record. Some storefronts send no star rating on search rows (on 19/10/2026, 21 of 21 rows in South Africa, `country=ZA`); when no app on the page has a rating, `_warnings` carries `ratings_unavailable`. `app.rating.count` and `app.reviews_count` come with the first row only (measured 21/11/2026: 1 of 20 rows), because the store search page shows the count for its top result alone; read /v1/google_play/app-info for the count of any other app. Served from the Google Play catalogue: a first, uncached call is task-polled upstream and typically takes 3 to 15s, with a review pull at high `depth` reaching 40s. Set a client timeout of at least 60s.

**Use when** you want to find an app's package name by keyword; description, screenshots, and install counts come from app-info.
**Cost** cache 120 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Paging** single page - Depth-based fan-out: page size is controlled by depth, one call.

**Query params**

- `query` (required) - Search keyword (e.g. 'photo editor'). · e.g. `photo editor`
- `country` (optional, string) - Storefront country as an ISO code ('US'), a full name ('United States'), or a numeric location code ('2840'). Defaults to the US, except that a query written in Hangul searches the Korean store (KR, ko) and one with Japanese kana the Japanese store (JP, ja) when neither `country` nor `language` is sent; `_warnings` says so. · e.g. `United States`
- `language` (optional, string) - Language code (e.g. 'en'). Defaults to 'en'.
- `depth` (optional, integer) - Number of results to retrieve (default 30, rounded up to multiples of 30, max 300). Note: Google Play's organic keyword search typically exposes only ~30 ranked results, so higher depth values rarely return more. To page deeper for app discovery, use /v1/google_play/app-listings-search (a filterable title/description database with real limit/offset/total). · e.g. `30`

**Response** `AppList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ app }` ([full schema](schemas/AppList.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `app.id` | Store app ID… |
| `app.title` | App title |
| `app.url` | URL of the app's store page. |
| `app.developer.id` | The store's id for the developer. |
| `app.developer.name` | Developer or publisher name. |
| `app.developer.url` | URL of the developer's page in the store. |

+23 more (types in the full schema): `app` {category, description, icon, minimum_os_version, released_at, reviews_count, size, store, subtitle, update_notes, updated_at, version}; `app.developer` {address, email, website}; `app.price` {currency, current, displayed, is_free} (+4 more). Page-level: `data.dropped`, `data.empty_reason`, `data.empty_reason_note`.

**Next** `google_play/app-info` (`app_id` ← `data.items[].app.id`) - Full details for each app. · `google_play/app-reviews` (`app_id` ← `data.items[].app.id`) - User reviews of each app.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/google_play/app-search" \
  --data-urlencode "query=photo editor" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/google_play/books/search - 1 credit (standard)

Returns Google Play books for a search, or a category's storefront shelves, on the canonical Product: Google Play's id for the book, title, link, description, price with the original price when it is reduced, currency, rating out of 5 and cover, with Google Play's own facts in product.ext.google_play (the search group or shelf in section, type ebook or audiobook, author, category, series position such as Book 4, and the prices as printed). A search answers ebooks and audiobooks together, about 20 of each; send type=ebook or type=audiobook for one of them and its next pages (about 50 a page) through the cursor. price narrows a search to free or paid books. category browses a category's shelves instead (for example coll_1689, children's books), one page, each book once with its first shelf; age (5_and_under, 6-8, 9-12) narrows the children's books category.

**Use when** you want to compare book prices, track a title or author on Google Play, or list a category's featured books.
**Cost** cache 120 s
**Empty results** An upstream 404 means "zero items", not "not found" - you get `200 {items: []}` and a refund.
**Paging** cursor · ≈20/page (observed once) · depth unknown · N items ≈ ceil(N/20) x 1 credits

**Query params**

- `query` (optional, string) - What to search for, up to 2,048 characters. Send query or category. · e.g. `atomic habits`
- `category` (optional, string) - Google Play's book category id to browse instead of searching, for example coll_1689 (children's books).
- `type` (optional, enum: ebook | audiobook) - ebook or audiobook: only that group of a search, with a cursor for its next pages.
- `age` (optional, enum: 5_and_under | 6-8 | 9-12) - 5_and_under, 6-8 or 9-12: narrows the children's books category (category=coll_1689).
- `price` (optional, enum: free | paid) - free or paid: narrows a book search (with query).
- `country` (optional, string) - Two-letter storefront country, for example us or gb (default us).
- `language` (optional, string) - Storefront language, for example en or de (default en).
- `cursor` (optional, string) - The next_cursor from a previous page of the same search, sent with the same type. Omit for the first page.
- **Shared controls** `max_pages` (1-50) → [walks](api-overview.md#search-filters-and-multi-page-walks); `max_items` (1-5000) · `max_credits` (1-100000) → [one-call walks](api-overview.md#get-more-in-one-call-max_items-max_credits-max_pages)

**Constraints**

- Provide at least one of `query`, `category`.

**Response** `ProductList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ product }` ([full schema](schemas/ProductList.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `product.title` | Product title |
| `product.id` | Platform product ID… |
| `product.url` | Direct URL to the product page |
| `product.description` | Product description. |
| `product.image_urls` | Primary image URL, or an array of image URLs for products… |
| `product.price.currency` | Currency code of the price. |

+3 more (types in the full schema): `product.price` {current, original}; `product.rating` {average}. Never filled: `product.availability`, `product.brand`, `product.rating.count`, `product.reviews_count`, `product.seller`. Empty on every row the field-health check sampled (22/11/2026), so not returned today: `product.ext.google_play`. Page-level: `data.dropped`, `data.empty_reason`, `data.empty_reason_note`, `data.walk`.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/google_play/books/search" \
  --data-urlencode "query=atomic habits" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/google_play/locations - 1 credit (standard)

Returns the Google Play storefronts (name + numeric location code + ISO country code) accepted by the `country` param on every google_play endpoint: 211 countries. Static reference data, heavily cached. Storefronts are country-level, so a sub-country code resolves to its parent and returns that country's data: `country=1019999` (a Minnesota city) and `country=US` returned byte-identical charts on 06/09/2026. `location_type=all` returns the full underlying geo tree instead, all 269,681 rows of it (cities, postal codes, neighbourhoods, airports), which is a 46 MB response and rarely what you want here.

**Use when** you want to find a valid value for the country parameter on the other Google Play endpoints.
**Cost** cache 1800 s
**Paging** none

**Query params**

- `location_type` (optional, enum: country | all) - `country` (default) returns the storefronts the `country` param accepts. `all` returns the full underlying geo tree, including cities, postal codes and neighbourhoods, which all resolve to their parent country. · e.g. `country`

**Response** `Analytics` rows at `data.items[]` (inferred from a sample): {location_code number, location_name string, location_name_parent null, country_iso_code string, location_type string}.

Page-level: `data.dropped`, `data.empty_reason`, `data.empty_reason_note`, `data.items`, `data.next_cursor`, `data.total`.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/google_play/locations" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/google_play/movies/search - 1 credit (standard)

Returns Google Play films and TV for a search, or a category's storefront shelves, on the canonical Product: Google Play's id for the title, title, link, description, price with the original price when it is reduced, currency, rating out of 5 and poster, with Google Play's own facts in product.ext.google_play (the search group or shelf in section, type movie, tv_show or tv_episode, category, content rating such as PG-13, trailer link, and the prices as printed). A search answers films, shows and episodes together; send type for one of them and its next pages through the cursor. category browses a category's shelves instead (for example FAMILY), one page, each title once with its first shelf; age (5_and_under, 6-8, 9-12) narrows the family films category.

**Use when** you want to compare rental and purchase prices, track a film on Google Play, or list a category's featured titles.
**Cost** cache 120 s
**Empty results** An upstream 404 means "zero items", not "not found" - you get `200 {items: []}` and a refund.
**Paging** cursor · ≈20/page (observed once) · depth unknown · N items ≈ ceil(N/20) x 1 credits

**Query params**

- `query` (optional, string) - What to search for, up to 2,048 characters. Send query or category. · e.g. `dune`
- `category` (optional, string) - Google Play's film category id to browse instead of searching, for example FAMILY.
- `type` (optional, enum: movie | tv_show | tv_episode) - movie, tv_show or tv_episode: only that group of a search, with a cursor for its next pages.
- `age` (optional, enum: 5_and_under | 6-8 | 9-12) - 5_and_under, 6-8 or 9-12: narrows the family films category (category=FAMILY).
- `country` (optional, string) - Two-letter storefront country, for example us or gb (default us).
- `language` (optional, string) - Storefront language, for example en or de (default en).
- `cursor` (optional, string) - The next_cursor from a previous page of the same search, sent with the same type. Omit for the first page.
- **Shared controls** `max_pages` (1-50) → [walks](api-overview.md#search-filters-and-multi-page-walks); `max_items` (1-5000) · `max_credits` (1-100000) → [one-call walks](api-overview.md#get-more-in-one-call-max_items-max_credits-max_pages)

**Constraints**

- Provide at least one of `query`, `category`.

**Response** `ProductList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ product }` ([full schema](schemas/ProductList.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `product.title` | Product title |
| `product.id` | Platform product ID… |
| `product.url` | Direct URL to the product page |
| `product.description` | Product description. |
| `product.image_urls` | Primary image URL, or an array of image URLs for products… |
| `product.price.currency` | Currency code of the price. |

+2 more (types in the full schema): `product.price` {current}; `product.rating` {average}. Never filled: `product.availability`, `product.brand`, `product.rating.count`, `product.reviews_count`, `product.seller`. Empty on every row the field-health check sampled (22/11/2026), so not returned today: `product.ext.google_play`, `product.price.original`. Page-level: `data.dropped`, `data.empty_reason`, `data.empty_reason_note`, `data.walk`.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/google_play/movies/search" \
  --data-urlencode "query=dune" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/google_play/search-suggestions - 1 credit (standard)

Returns Google Play's search autocomplete suggestions for a keyword stem: the same terms the store's search box surfaces. The day Play starts autocompleting a phrase, real demand exists; poll a stem daily and diff to catch rising app keywords early. Each item is `{ term, priority }` ranked by Play's own order (Play exposes no numeric score). Returns a list under `items`.

**Use when** you want it for store keyword research: poll a stem daily and diff the list to catch rising app searches early.
**Cost** cache 120 s
**Paging** single page - Play's autocomplete returns one fixed block of suggestions and exposes no cursor, offset or size parameter.

**Query params**

- `query` (required) - Partial search keyword to autocomplete (e.g. 'reverse'). · e.g. `reverse`
- `country` (optional, string) - ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 storefront country code (e.g. 'us', 'gb', 'kr'). Defaults to 'us'. Anything that is not alpha-2 is rejected with a free 400; an unrecognised alpha-2 code is forwarded, and Google Play answers it with its default storefront rather than an error, so check the code if results look wrong for the market. · e.g. `us`
- `language` (optional, string) - ISO 639-1 language code. Defaults to 'en'. · e.g. `en`

**Response** `SearchResult` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ term, priority }` (inferred from a sample): {term string, priority number}.

Page-level: `data.dropped`, `data.empty_reason`, `data.empty_reason_note`.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/google_play/search-suggestions" \
  --data-urlencode "query=reverse" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```
